findings.text: the bound is measured false in the wide direction: with the identity exported at the feature commit, three files that never name the three variables also go red for the same reason — tests/test_mcp_roadmap.py 5 failures, tests/test_plan_summary_bound.py 2, tests/test_mcp_views.py 1 — and are green with the identity cleared in the same tree (c1: 71 passed, the one failure a scratch-tree artifact), so the ambient-sensitive population is 80 failures over six files, not 72 over three, and the autouse fixture covers all of it: the head arm over the same 36 files with the identity still exported is 1 failed / 430 passed / 7 skipped (w2b), the one failure pre-existing at the pristine base (c2).

item_verdicts.diff: the diff implements the refusal and the run-worktree resolution in reckon/mcp.py behind `checkout_path is None` (RUN_ID_ENV at reckon/mcp.py:423, _run_scoped_checkout at reckon/mcp.py:476, the guard at reckon/mcp.py:2827, the hint path at reckon/mcp.py:416), leaves the coordinator and explicit-checkout_path paths unchanged, and adds the autouse monkeypatch-scoped isolation fixture that removes exactly the three variables a dispatch exports, with the new test covering the unreadable-pointer branch the previous review found untested.
item_verdicts.done_when: the gate the run recorded does assert the done-when and its figures reproduced here to the failure count — my seven-file head arm is 179 passed with the identity exported (r2), my seven-file feature-commit arm is 72 failed / 106 passed (r1, the recorded 107 counting its own five-test file against my four), and the fixture's necessity is falsified rather than assumed, since the same probe file is green where the fixture is present and red where only the fixture is missing (c3 versus c4).
item_verdicts.goal: the run-scoped plan write works as the goal states and was re-measured independently: with RECKON_RUN_ID exported, as it is in every worker's shell, the seven declared files read 179 passed / 0 failed at the reviewed head and 72 failed / 106 passed at the feature commit 22ae76dc under the same variable, and the question this review was asked to add — whether the autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py hides anything a test in this repository relies on — answers no: git grep at the head blob 8c43366a names the three variables in exactly four test files, of which conftest.py is the fixture itself, test_plan_write_stays_in_the_worktree.py sets its own run id per test and deletes it in the coordinator case, test_worker_env_export.py asserts on the environment dict dispatch builds rather than on ambient os.environ, and test_worker_stop_hook.py deletes the manifest at lines 162 and 320 to exercise the pointer fallback, so the fixture's removal is what those tests already arrange for themselves, and the removal is the fixture's doing rather than the shell's, shown by a probe that passes at the head (c3, 1 passed) and fails on the pre-fixture tree in the same ambient shell (c4, 1 failed).
item_verdicts.manifest: the manifest's status and figures are accurate where checked, and it states its own deviation honestly (the declared measure names three red-at-base tests and only the two new-behaviour tests are, repeated at docs/plans/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home.html:400), but its stated evidence bound under-describes the affected population by half a measure and no merged-head suite run backs the coverage claim, which is the single finding below.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the delivered work sits inside the declared paths except tests/conftest.py, which the record names as its single blocker, `reckon crew check-manifest` reports exactly that one finding and no other, the landing record states why the path was needed and why the run could not widen its own fence (docs/evidence/archive/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home-landed.html:838), and the promotion instruction is carried, so the crossing is visible rather than silent; nothing else in the delivery departs from the declared scope.

justifications.durability: five tests pin the contract through the public entry, the new one closes the unreadable-pointer branch (tests/test_plan_write_stays_in_the_worktree.py:148), and the fixture carries its own falsifier, c4-identity-probe-prefixture.log red where c3-identity-probe-head.log is green in the same shell.
justifications.evidence: every recorded arm reproduced here to the failure count (72/106 at 22ae76dc, 179/0 at head) and each of my logs names its tree, revision and imported module path, but the bound at manifest.md:29 covers only the declared selection plus the files that name the variables, and the ambient-sensitive set is wider, so the record's own stated bound is measured false in the wide direction.
justifications.fit: symbols name the mechanism rather than the plan (RUN_ID_ENV, _run_scoped_checkout, without_dispatch_identity), no plan or ticket label appears in the change, the fixture reuses the repo's existing monkeypatch-scoped autouse idiom, and the module docstring states the failure the change prevents.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the contract is exercised through the same entry production uses (mcp_module._edit_plan with checkout_path=None) and the main checkout's bytes are asserted unchanged, tests/test_plan_write_stays_in_the_worktree.py:109 and :131, so a write that reached main could not pass while reporting success.
justifications.scope_discipline: one path outside the fence, tests/conftest.py, review-directed, disclosed at docs/evidence/archive/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home-landed.html:838-844 with the promotion instruction, and the run's audit reports that single finding; the rest of the delivery is inside the declared paths.
